title: Quantifying the Environmental Sustainability of the Nursery Shrimp Farm: A Case Study in India
content:
Environmental impacts of a nursery shrimp farm in India were quantified using life cycle assessment. Key environmental hotspots were identified, feed and electricity scenarios were tested to support more sustainable production.


ABSTRACT

Nursery shrimp production is a critical but resource-intensive stage in the shrimp production lifecycle, where post-larvae are reared under controlled conditions until stocking size. Although typically operated as a closed system, nursery production requires substantial material and energy inputs, raising concerns regarding its environmental sustainability. This study evaluates the environmental performance of a commercial shrimp nursery farm in India using a cradle-to-gate attributional life cycle assessment with a functional unit of 1000 juvenile shrimp produced at the farm gate. In addition to the base case, scenario simulations assessed the effects of alternative feed formulations and energy sources as potential mitigation strategies. Results identified feed and electricity as the two dominant contributors. For the base case, feed accounted for 98% of land use and 77% of ecosystem damage, while electricity accounted for 48% of the 100-year global warming potential and 53% of the human health endpoint. Concrete was the principal infrastructure contributor, accounting for 16%–23% of impacts. In the scenario simulations, doubling fishmeal inclusion in the feed by halving the soybean meal reduced land use by 44% and ecosystem damage by 29%, but increased resource use by 9% and cumulative energy demand by 4%, indicating a trade-off. Substituting half of the grid electricity with concentrated solar power reduced the human health endpoint by 24%, the 100-year global warming potential by 23% and freshwater eutrophication by 34%. This study provides the first comprehensive life cycle assessment of shrimp nursery production and establishes a benchmark to support targeted sustainability improvements within shrimp supply chains.
